statement.p: Find the limit of the function f(x,y) = \frac{\sin(5\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right))}{5\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)} as (x,y) \to (0,0). Assume that polynomials, exponentials, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions are continuous. [Hint: \lim_{t\to 0}\frac{\sin t}{t}=1.]

p.em: (Enter DNE if the limit does not exist.)

static.solution: \lim_{(x,y)\to(0,0)} f(x,y) = \lim_{(x,y)\to(0,0)}\frac{\sin(5\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right))}{5\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)}. As r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2} is the distance from (x,y) to (0,0) we have that (x,y) \to (0,0) is equivalent to r \to 0. Hence the limit becomes: \lim_{(x,y)\to(0,0)}f(x,y) = \lim _{r\to0}\frac{\sin 5r^{2}}{5r^{2}} = 1.
